extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.22651v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by extracting visual and auditory inputs from 37 (to 47) source datasets spanning audio understanding, text benchmarks, and visual reasoning. Role profiles and questions were taken from RoleBench with representative audio clips collected per role. Speech instructions were synthesized from text using three text-to-speech (TTS) models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B), evaluated using UTMOS (regenerating if below 3.8), and transcribed with Whisper to retain only audio recordings with the lowest word error rates.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Extracted from 47 source datasets, including MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTG-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIC-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, and MyST.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were preprocessed prior to speech synthesis by replacing special tokens (such as '<image1>') with descriptive phrases, rewriting texts via Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to enhance TTS readability for numbers/math expressions, rephrasing multiple-choice options, and reusing 300 role audio clips from the role-play task as prompt audio.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance matching to flag and manually remove duplicate questions; (2) Validation discarding roughly 10% of candidates with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, or demonstrably incorrect answers; (3) Categorization into 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; and (4) Sampling to balance category representation, resulting in 10,497 items.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual curation and validation were conducted via a lightweight web-based tool. Curators performed a three-pass review: checking media integrity (audible, visible, non-corrupted), checking task well-posedness (clear, unambiguous prompts and matching options), and verifying answer validity and multi-turn coherence, subsequently assigning a 'Good' or 'Bad' verdict along with optional notes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A lightweight web-based curation tool with inline players and viewers, transcripts, and multiple-choice options.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement and stability were analyzed via human evaluation validation comparing automated gpt-oss-20b judgments against independent human ratings on a 10% sample (1,050 examples), yielding Pearson correlation coefficients between 0.73 and 1.00 (overall 0.92) and an overall human agreement rate of 96.1%. Repeated scoring runs across ten iterations were used to verify evaluation stability.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B, UTMOS, Whisper-Large-v3, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, gpt-oss-20b, emotion2vec, Wespeaker
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Authors commit to maintaining a data governance process for auditing and removal, reserving the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender, vocal timbre/speaker identities (role audio from 100 roles), user emotions (7 user emotions evaluated: angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, surprised), and speech recordings.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables evaluation and development of hands-free voice AI assistants for healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, automotive, and accessibility (assisting visually impaired users). Includes evaluation of potential safety risks, malicious queries, and ethical behavior to minimize harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, harassment, fraud, and unequal demographic performance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The questions and contexts are derived from academic or synthetic sources and rewritten instructions, which may not reflect real deployments; the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and style prompts that may encode stereotypes or omit user personas; and the dataset is predominantly English (with only five Chinese roles in roleplay), potentially lacking diversity across linguistic settings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is predominantly monolingual (English, with only five Chinese roles); evaluation focuses heavily on open-source models with only one proprietary model tested; automated evaluation using LLM-as-a-judge (gpt-oss-20b) may introduce bias or favor specific phrasings; dynamic/continuous streaming interaction tasks (live audio streams or video narratives) are not covered; and the evaluation is conducted offline and statically, without measuring real-time deployment factors such as latency, barge-in (interruption), partial utterances, or error recovery.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating large language and multimodal models across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. Intended specifically for evaluation; not intended to be used as training data.
